context: A consolidation mandate whose selection argument is a single headline number that the fixtures disprove. Predicted baseline failure: the agent treats the 99.6% / 91.2% / 88.0% green-rate table in notes/consolidation-memo.md as reliability evidence and either adopts the admin stack outright or, having decided against it, still concedes that the admin suite is the most stable of the three. It is neither. apps/admin/cypress.config.ts sets retries to 4 in run mode and 2 in open mode, and reports/admin-e2e-2026-09-08.log is a green run in which six tests pass only on attempt 2, 3, 4 or 5 - a revoked-member test taking 61.9 seconds across four attempts and a credit-note test 98 seconds across five - while apps/storefront/playwright.config.ts retries once, only in CI. The two numbers are not measuring the same thing: 99.6% is what four retries buys, and every one of those late passes is a flake candidate nobody is triaging because the job never goes red. The second predicted failure is the language axis. Ola proposes the five Python-writing integrations engineers pick up TypeScript as they go, and the platform reply proposes the opposite escape - move all three suites onto the Selenium Grid because 'the only thing that takes TypeScript and Python over one protocol is WebDriver' - which is false, and taking it expands a manual-synchronisation stack the partner-portal test already shows (a bare time.sleep(5) before a WebDriverWait) across the whole company. Both wrong paths are attractive: one has the VP's number and an 18-month contract behind it, the other has idle hardware and hurts nobody's feelings. The agent is further predicted to name a tool without scoring a single axis, to accept the memo's line that the node --test unit suite belongs in the browser runner, and to say nothing about the CI shape the platform pair asked for - the 41-minute single job walking three browsers across two environments, and the credentials sitting in apps/admin/cypress.env.json. A flat refusal that prices nothing is the mirror-image failure: the consolidation across the three browser suites is real and she needs it costed.

checklist.name: Both documents produced with a per-suite table
checklist.description: docs/consolidation-response.md and docs/tooling-by-area.md both exist, and the second has one row per suite that runs today - storefront e2e, storefront unit, admin e2e, partner portal e2e - each naming its tool. A table that collapses the suites into a single row, or omits the unit suite, scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT treat the admin suite's green rate as reliability evidence
checklist.description: MUST NOT select a tool on the strength of the 99.6% figure, and MUST NOT carry apps/admin/cypress.config.ts's retry settings into whatever becomes the standard. Doing either scores zero for this criterion regardless of which tool is finally named - including an answer that rejects the admin stack for other reasons while still conceding it is the most stable of the three. Full marks require all of: naming retries runMode 4 as what produces the number, citing the late-attempt passes in reports/admin-e2e-2026-09-08.log as the proof, stating that the three green rates are not comparable because storefront retries once and only in CI, and stating the convention the standard should hold to - at most one retry, in CI only, with anything that passes on a later attempt raised as a flake candidate rather than absorbed. Spotting the retry setting but still repeating the green-rate ranking, or doubting the number without locating why it is wrong, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT strand the Python team on a single-language runner
checklist.description: MUST NOT put services/partner-portal on a runner that only takes JavaScript and TypeScript. Naming one for that row scores zero here, and so does adopting Ola's line that five integrations engineers pick up TypeScript as they go. Full marks require the language axis to be named as a selection constraint and answered concretely: either the recommended runner has an official binding in the language those five already write, identified as such, or the retraining is committed to and costed in engineer-weeks against the fact that nobody is hired before March. Noticing the mismatch and leaving the partner portal on its own separate tool - which abandons the consolidation for that area rather than solving it - scores at most half.

checklist.name: Grid-for-everyone refused and its premise corrected
checklist.description: The platform reply's proposal - put all three suites on the existing Selenium Grid because WebDriver is the only protocol that takes both languages - is refused, and its premise is corrected rather than merely overruled: a runner with first-party bindings in several languages exists, so multi-language does not force WebDriver. The refusal also names what expanding that stack costs, with the manual synchronisation in services/partner-portal/tests/test_partner_export.py (a fixed time.sleep before the explicit wait) as the visible instance. Recommending the Grid as the company standard scores zero. Rejecting it only because it is old, with no correction of the language premise, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Axes scored before any tool is named
checklist.description: The response scores the decision against named axes - browser scope, the language each team already writes, execution speed against the wall-clock figures in notes/ci-inventory-2026-09.md, ecosystem, and how hireable the result is - before recommending anything, and ties each area's row back to those scores. Naming tools with no axes scored anywhere scores zero; listing axes but never applying them to a specific area scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT fold the unit suite into the browser runner
checklist.description: MUST NOT recommend moving apps/storefront/tests/unit off node --test into the end-to-end runner, however tidy 'one command is the whole quality story' sounds - a 40-second in-process unit suite and a browser suite are different layers and the mandate does not reach across them. Recommending the move scores zero. Leaving the unit suite alone with no reason given scores at most half.

checklist.name: The consolidation that is real is carried out and priced
checklist.description: The browser suites that genuinely can converge do converge in the recommendation, and per-area migration cost is given in engineer-weeks with the losses listed per area rather than in general. An answer that refuses every proposal and prices nothing scores zero - she has a board pack in January and a position with no numbers in it is the outcome she has already rejected three times.

checklist.name: CI shape stated for the consolidated suite
checklist.description: The platform pair are told what the pipeline looks like afterwards, concretely: the suite sharded to a single-digit-minute wall clock rather than the current 41-minute run, one job per browser and environment cell instead of the sequential loop in .github/workflows/admin-e2e.yml, and the credentials in apps/admin/cypress.env.json moved into the CI secret store instead of travelling with the migration. Saying nothing about the pipeline scores zero; naming one of the three scores at most half.
